Hi Tessa,

Thanks for the quick sync earlier. As we finalize the contract, procurement has asked for a concise mutual action plan that includes the performance evaluation scope and an acceptance checklist. Primary asks from our side:

- Clear definitions for TTFT (time to first token), p50/p95 latency, and steady-state throughput metrics.
- Concurrency scenarios: expected steady-state (100–200 concurrent sessions) and burst probes (up to 800 concurrent sessions for short windows).
- How you’ll measure queueing/backpressure and what the graceful degradation looks like.
- Any adjustments to rate limits/routing you recommend for production.

We need a MAP + test plan by EOD next Tuesday (May 10) so our engineering and procurement teams can greenlight the SOW. Also, please confirm any platform or access requirements you need from our side (test API keys, sample prompts, dataset slices).

Appreciate it — Alice
Director of Engineering
FintechCo

From: tessa_morgan <tessa@redwood.ai>

Date: 2027-05-03 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP / performance scope for go‑live

Hi Alice — great summary. We’ll deliver a MAP+benchmark plan that covers all items below; attaching an initial draft (FintechCo_MAP_v1.xlsx). High level plan:

1) Definitions and acceptance criteria
   - TTFT: measured from request ingestion to first token emitted by the model (p50/p95 targets).
   - Latency: p50/p95 for end-to-end response (including network + queuing).
   - Throughput: sustained tokens/sec under steady-state load.

2) Concurrency scenarios
   - Steady-state: 150 concurrent sessions (baseline), run for 2 hours to validate KV cache hit behavior.
   - Burst probes: 5-minute ramp to 800 concurrent sessions to observe queueing and failed request rate.

3) Queueing & backpressure observation
   - Instrument queue depth, request wait time, and per-route drop rate.
   - Run with incremental rate-limit settings to identify knee points.

4) Rate-limit tuning recommendations
   - Start with soft token-bucket limits (burst capacity = 3x steady tokens) and backoff policy for clients.

5) Test artifacts and deliverables
   - Benchmark runbook (run commands, datasets), raw logs, perf-summary.pdf with charts, and a short executive slide.

Proposed schedule:
   - Draft MAP (attached) sent today
   - Pilot burst probe: Mon May 10 09:00–10:00 PT
   - Steady-state validation: Wed May 12 01:00–03:00 PT
   - Consolidated results and recommended config: Fri May 14

Can you confirm Procure/Eng availability for the May 10 pilot window? Also flag any compliance or IP restrictions for logs.

Thanks — Tessa
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference

Hi Alice / team — quick post-pilot summary and recommended changes before the steady‑state run. Pilot details: 2027-05-10 09:00 PT, burst probe sequence executed per matrix. Deliverables attached: perf-summary.pdf, logs.tar.gz (masked).

Executive highlights:
- TTFT (p95): 380ms during steady warmed runs; p50 ~120ms.
- End-to-end latency (p95): steady-state 980ms; during burst peaks observed up to 2.1s for <2% of requests.
- Throughput: steady-state sustained ~85 tokens/sec per instance; aggregated throughput matched expected scaling at 150 concurrent sessions.
- Burst behavior: queue depth spiked during 30–90s after ramp; observed queue-induced wait time up to 600ms at peak. No systemic errors; retry rate rose to ~1.6% under the highest probe (800 conc.).

Recommendations to include in MAP before go‑live:
1) Rate-limit tuning: set soft token-bucket to 3x steady throughput and enable 429 with exponential jitter.
2) Autoscaling: reduce scale-out threshold from 75% to 65% GPU utilization for the first 72 hours post-deploy to reduce queuing risk.
3) Fallbacks: pre-configure a smaller model variant and enable automatic routing for latency-critical routes if p95 > 1.5s for >5 minutes.
4) Observability: retain masked logs for 90 days; provide an ops dashboard with live queue depth and retry metrics.

Next steps: we’ll run the steady-state validation May 12–13 as planned and provide a final perf summary by May 17 that you can attach to the SOW. If procurement signs off on the test addendum, lab will keep the burst pool available.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this out.

— Tessa
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
